subject: Honor notifications/cancelled in the orchestra-engine MCP server

seed.consequence: The untouched launcher contracts in packs/codex/agents/executor-codex.md, executor-codex-heavy.md, reviewer-codex.md and architect-codex.md key their one permitted re-issue off whether the MCP TRANSPORT ERROR shows captured runner output ("if the transport error instead shows captured runner output, the runner DID run — relay the error verbatim and stop"), and because the runners emit their report only at the end, a cancelled run's streams are normally empty, so the cancellation notice now carries no stdout/stderr block at all and the launcher reads it as the "runner never launched" exception and re-issues the exec call once — starting a second, unaudited engine over the very working tree that same message declared possibly HALF-EDITED.
seed.rationale: Omitting an empty stream tail reads as harmless tidying inside a brand-new message block, and nothing in the touched files depends on it — the block's real job is to be the machine-visible evidence, for a consumer outside the diff, that a process actually ran. Suppressing it silently flips that consumer's retry decision on the one path where a retry is most destructive.
hazard_terms: contract change whose only consumer sits outside the diff
message shape a caller keys its branch off
conditionally omitted field read as absence of evidence

design_note: The commit's cancellation notice is a new message with a fixed shape, and the launcher agents that consume it — none of them touched here — decide whether a stopped call may be re-issued from whether that message shows captured runner output. The injection makes the stdout/stderr tails conditional on those streams being non-empty, which is locally the most reasonable-looking line in the block and is invisible to the suite (the cancellation fixture writes nothing to either stream, so both tails were "(empty)" at C anyway). Finding it requires leaving the two touched files and reading the launcher contract that consumes the message.
